title: Whole-exome sequencing in individuals with obsessive-compulsive disorder and chronic tic disorders identifies 36 large-effect risk genes
authors: Belinda Wang; Matthew N. Tran; Sheng Wang; et al.
evidence_type: peer-reviewed primary human genetic association study
date_caveat: October 26 publicity led to discovery of an older September paper; not new-window evidence.
population: Affected OCD, chronic tic disorder or combined probands; no persistent-severe-adult-specific estimate extracted.
design: Whole-exome association analyses, including previously reported samples; not an independent replication of every contributing cohort.
interpretation: Combined and diagnosis-specific analyses contribute to the 36-gene union; 34 is the combined-analysis count. Gene associations are not validated treatment targets or individual prognoses.
outcome: Rare-variant genetic association, not clinical response or functional improvement.
precision: Gene-specific effect intervals not extracted; no pooled clinical effect calculated.
risk_of_bias: Selected ascertainment and reused cohorts limit independent-replication interpretation
No age-, severity- or communication-group clinical validation established by this extraction
funding_conflicts: Not extracted in this bounded abstract/main-text pass.
claim_supported: Older primary association evidence adds mechanistic hypotheses.
claim_not_supported: A deterministic cause for every person, personal genetic risk, treatment efficacy or cure.
access: Primary abstract and opening main-text paragraphs inspected; full methods, supplements and individual variant data not inspected or retained.
reviewer: AI-assisted extraction with independent source check
correction_retraction_check: No linked notice in current PubMed metadata.
next_verification_task: If prioritized later, inspect aggregate ancestry, ascertainment, sample overlap and gene-specific uncertainty before stronger translation claims.
